title: Tomini Elettrici
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Small, fresh Piedmontese cheese rounds marinated in a fiery chili-spiked olive oil, their playful name meaning 'electric,' a nod to the noticeable heat that builds with each bite.
longDesc: Tomini are simple, mild fresh cheeses on their own, but marinating them in a punchy blend of chili, garlic, and vinegar transforms them into a lively appetizer that has become a popular modern feature on Piedmontese antipasto boards.
ingredients: 8 small tomini cheeses (or substitute small rounds of fresh mild cheese)
150 ml (2/3 cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Arrange the tomini cheeses in a single layer in a shallow dish.
Whisk together the olive oil, vinegar, chopped chilies, garlic, parsley, and a pinch of salt.
Pour the marinade evenly over the cheeses.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight, turning occasionally.
Bring to room temperature before serving.
Serve with plenty of the chili-infused oil spooned over.
chefTips: Adjust the amount of chili to your heat preference - the dish is meant to have a noticeable kick, but the intensity is flexible.
Letting the cheese marinate overnight allows the flavors to penetrate more deeply.
Bringing the cheese to room temperature before serving lets its flavor and the marinade aroma come through fully.
commonMistakes: Serving straight from the refrigerator, which mutes both the cheese and marinade flavors.
Using overly aged or strong cheese, which can clash with the delicate fresh tomini character this dish is built around.
Not marinating long enough, missing the full infusion of chili and garlic flavor.
storage: Refrigerate in the marinade for up to 5 days.
reheating: Not applicable; served cold or at room temperature.
healthBenefits: A good source of calcium and protein from the fresh cheese.
culturalNote: Tomini elettrici is a modern, popular addition to Piedmontese antipasto spreads, its playful heat a fun contrast to the region's more traditional, gentler appetizers.
